artifacts.notes: Exact dated Tertullian Project delivery of sermons 99-109. Extent as measured by the retrieving lane: complete tertullian.org file for Cyril of Alexandria, Commentary on Luke, Sermons 99-109 (Luke 13:22-16:13), carrying Payne Smith's printed page numbers |461 to |516 inline; Sermons 101 and 102, the two that treat the appointed Gospel, are entire within it. The sibling delivery of sermons 110-123 registered on this same edition in July 2026 stands `remote` and `restricted` on the ground that the host's transcription was "not assumed redistributable"; the express public-domain dedication quoted in `rights_basis` was read off these bytes and off the site's own index page rather than assumed, which is why this artifact is retained and that one was not. The disagreement is between an assumption and a reading, and it is left visible rather than resolved by editing the older record. The host modernises the English of the 1859 printing and interleaves Payne Smith's printed page numbers as |461 to |516, so this is a checked English witness and not a facsimile.
artifacts.rights_basis: The host states the basis on the page itself. The Tertullian Project's index of these files prints, over the whole collection, "These English translations are all out of copyright, but were not included in the 38 volume collection of Ante-Nicene, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers. Please take copies and place online elsewhere. In some cases I have felt it necessary to add an introduction to the online text. These are all placed in the public domain also -- copy freely.", and the foot of this very file prints "This text was transcribed by Roger Pearse, 2008. All material on this page is in the public domain - copy freely." Payne Smith's 1859 translation is separately in the United States public domain by publication date. The host's transcription, its editor's own added matter and its markup are therefore covered by an express public-domain dedication in the source's own words, quoted here rather than inferred, and the file is retained.

alternate_titles: Homilies on the Gospel of Saint Luke
work.author: Cyril of Alexandria
work.description: Cyril of Alexandria's homiletic commentary on Luke, surviving substantially in a Syriac version and partly in Greek catena fragments. It is conventionally cited by sermon number; sermons 4 and 5 treat the Presentation in the Temple and the finding of the boy Jesus.
work.title: Commentary on the Gospel of Saint Luke
